package_info.package_manager: N/A (malware distributed via bundling/drive-by-downloads, not a package manager)
package_info.why_malicious: Fireball is a browser hijacker with remote control capabilities, designed to take over browsers, manipulate web traffic, and generate advertisement revenue. It is distributed without user consent, can execute arbitrary code received from a remote server, and enables large-scale ad fraud as well as potential further compromise of infected systems by providing persistent attacker control.

execution_context.trigger: At browser launch or system startup
execution_context.file_location: Injected into the browser process memory or installed as a browser extension/add-on (e.g., Chrome/Firefox extension directory, or via DLL injection for IE/Edge)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At browser launch or system startup, the code modifies browser settings to set a malicious homepage and search engine, injects advertisements into web pages by altering page content, monitors user browsing activity, and executes code received from a remote C&C server, resulting in persistent browser hijacking, ad fraud, user tracking, and enabling further remote compromise.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code forcibly changes browser settings, injects unauthorized advertisements, monitors user activity, and allows execution of remote payloads, all without user consent. These actions are characteristic of browser hijackers and adware, and enable both financial fraud and further system compromise.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate browser extensions or software should not alter browser settings, inject ads, or execute remote code without explicit user or administrator permission. Normal software does not establish persistent unauthorized control over browser configuration or user activity.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Enterprise browser management tools may set homepage or search engine, but only with user or admin consent, and never inject ads or execute arbitrary remote code. Security or monitoring tools may observe user activity, but with clear disclosure and consent.
key_indicators: Unauthorized modification of browser homepage and search engine settings
Injection of third-party advertisements into web pages
Execution of code or scripts received from remote C&C servers
Persistence mechanisms such as registry modification, startup folder entries, or scheduled tasks
Monitoring and exfiltration of user browsing activity

attack_chain.action: User unknowingly installs Fireball via bundled software or drive-by-download, often without clear notification or consent.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malware is present on the system and is configured to execute at browser launch or system startup.

attack_chain.action: Fireball modifies browser settings to hijack the homepage and search engine, injects advertisements into web pages, and establishes persistence.
attack_chain.leads_to: User web traffic is redirected to attacker-controlled domains and monetized through ad fraud, while the malware remains active across reboots.

attack_chain.action: Fireball establishes communication with a remote C&C server, monitors user activity, and can execute arbitrary code or payloads received from the attacker.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker can further compromise the system, exfiltrate data, or use the infected host for additional malicious activities.

behavioral_signatures: Unauthorized modification of browser homepage and search engine settings (e.g., changes to prefs.js, registry, or browser config files)
Injection of advertisements or scripts into web pages not present in original content
Browser extension or process making unexpected outbound connections to known ad fraud or C&C domains
Execution of code or scripts received from remote servers within the browser context
Persistence mechanisms such as new startup entries, scheduled tasks, or registry modifications related to browser processes
file_indicators: Presence of unknown or suspicious browser extensions/add-ons in browser extension directories
Unexpected changes in browser configuration files (e.g., prefs.js for Firefox, registry keys for IE/Edge/Chrome)
New or modified files in browser extension/add-on folders with obfuscated or unsigned code
Persistence mechanisms in startup folders, scheduled tasks, or registry Run/RunOnce keys
network_indicators: Outbound connections to known Fireball C&C or ad fraud domains (e.g., http://malicious-ad-domain.com, or domains listed in threat intelligence feeds)
Frequent HTTP requests from browser processes to domains not associated with user activity or legitimate browsing
Unusual traffic patterns or spikes in outbound connections from browser processes, especially after startup
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for unauthorized changes to browser settings (homepage, search engine) by auditing browser configuration files and registry keys. Detect installation of unknown or unsigned browser extensions/add-ons. Analyze browser process network activity for connections to known malicious or ad fraud domains. Correlate browser process activity with file system and network events to identify ad injection, persistence mechanisms, and remote code execution attempts. Use endpoint security tools and threat intelligence to flag known Fireball indicators and behaviors.
